title: Claim: Home Ministry Agniveer portal data offered for sale, Mathrubhumi and Deshbandhu report; no official confirmation
date_note: Mathrubhumi English published it on 21 November (Malayalam edition 22 November); it says the listing came to light in September during Delhi Police dark web surveillance and gives no arrest date or earlier disclosure day.
place: India (country as stated; location of the portal not given)
geo_basis: country level; Delhi Police named as the investigator, no victim site location stated
summary: Mathrubhumi, citing unnamed official sources, reports Delhi Police apprehended a 14-year-old for allegedly hacking an MHA ex-Agniveer career portal and offering over 2,500 personnel records and admin credentials for $500. Deshbandhu, citing police officials, says Delhi Police's IFSO unit caught him in Ballabgarh, Haryana, holding data on about four thousand Agniveers, whose authenticity police are still verifying. Mathrubhumi's Malayalam edition says there is no official confirmation.
plain: An Indian newspaper reports police caught a teenager who allegedly advertised Agniveer recruits' personal details for sale. The Home Ministry has not confirmed it, and it is unclear whether the data is genuine.
exec: Unconfirmed report of defence-recruit personal data offered for sale; the Home Ministry has not confirmed it.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Mathrubhumi says Delhi Police reported the case to the Home Ministry.
impact: Mathrubhumi: personal records of over 2,500 Agniveer personnel; Deshbandhu: data on about four thousand Agniveers; authenticity not confirmed.

validation.note: Two publishers, Mathrubhumi (English 21 Nov, Malayalam 22 Nov) and Deshbandhu (Hindi, 22 Nov), both on unnamed police or official sources; figures differ (over 2,500 vs about four thousand). Mathrubhumi Malayalam says no official confirmation; Deshbandhu says police are still verifying authenticity. No Delhi Police or MHA statement read.
